misconception: Thinking that a bigger denominator means a bigger fraction
explanation: When you have the same numerator (1), a larger denominator means the whole is cut into more pieces, so each piece is smaller. 1/2 is one piece out of two, which is bigger than 1/4, which is one piece out of four.
reteach_method: Show a pizza or chocolate bar and cut it into halves and quarters. Ask the student to pick the larger piece. Then let them color the two halves and four quarters to see that the half covers more area than a quarter.

misconception: I think the fraction with a larger denominator (like 1/4) is bigger.
explanation: When the numerator is the same, a smaller denominator means each part is larger. 1/2 means one whole divided into two parts, so each part is bigger than one part when the whole is divided into four parts (1/4). Therefore 1/2 is greater than 1/4.
reteach_method: Draw a circle or a chocolate bar. Cut it into two equal pieces to show 1/2. Then cut the same circle into four equal pieces to show 1/4. Compare the size of one piece from each cut. You can also write 1/2 as 2/4 and see that 2/4 > 1/4.

misconception: Thinking that a fraction with a larger denominator is bigger
explanation: When the top number (numerator) is the same, the fraction with the smaller denominator is actually larger. For example, if you split a pizza into 2 equal parts, each part is bigger than if you split it into 4 equal parts.
reteach_method: Draw two circles, shade half of one and a quarter of the other. Then use a number line to show which fraction lies farther to the right.

misconception: You thought the fraction with the smaller denominator (1/2) was smaller, but actually a smaller denominator makes a bigger fraction.
explanation: Think of a circle split into equal parts. With 2 parts, each part is bigger than a part split into 3 parts. So 1/2 (half of a circle) is bigger than 1/3 (one third of a circle).
reteach_method: Draw two circles: cut one into 2 equal pieces and color one piece, then cut another into 3 equal pieces and color one piece. Compare the sizes of the colored parts to see which one is bigger.

misconception: You think the fraction with the bigger number below (denominator) is the larger one.
explanation: A fraction represents a part of a whole. If the denominator is bigger, the part is smaller. 1/2 is one half of a whole, which is 0.5. 1/4 is one quarter of a whole, which is 0.25. 0.5 is bigger than 0.25, so 1/2 is greater than 1/4.
reteach_method: Draw a number line or use a fraction bar. Shade one half and one quarter of the same shape. The half will stretch farther across the shape than the quarter, showing that 1/2 is larger.

misconception: Thinking that a fraction with a smaller denominator (like 1/2) is smaller than one with a larger denominator (like 1/3).
explanation: The denominator tells how many equal parts the whole is divided into. A larger denominator means each part is smaller. So when you split a whole into 3 parts (1/3), each part is smaller than when you split it into only 2 parts (1/2).
reteach_method: Draw a circle and cut it into 2 equal pieces. Then cut a new circle into 3 equal pieces. Compare the sizes of the pieces. You’ll see the piece from the 3‑cut is smaller than the piece from the 2‑cut.
